title: Optimizing Access in Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy as a Resource-Efficient Alternative to Conventional Schedules

sections.title: 研究问题
sections.text:
《Optimizing Access in Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy as a Resource-Efficient Alternative to Conventional Schedules》：研究问题的原文依据。

【Purpose · abstract-1-1】Concomitant chemoradiation therapy (cCRT) is a standard-of-care treatment option for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, improving locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS). However, many patients are unfit for cCRT and receive sequential chemoradiation therapy (sCRT); in this setting, hypofractionated radiation therapy may reduce treatment time, counter tumor repopulation, and improve access.

【Methods and materials · abstract-2-1】We retrospectively analyzed outcomes and prognostic factors among 131 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated at a single high-volume cancer center with 1 of 3 approaches: cCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-C; n = 52), sCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-S; n = 37), or sCRT with hypofractionation (HYPO-S; n = 42).

evidence.text: We retrospectively analyzed outcomes and prognostic factors among 131 patients with locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer treated at a single high-volume cancer center with 1 of 3 approaches: cCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-C; n = 52), sCRT with conventional fractionation (CONV-S; n = 37), or sCRT with hypofractionation (HYPO-S; n = 42).

Concomitant chemoradiation therapy (cCRT) is a standard-of-care treatment option for locally advanced non-small cell lung cancer, improving locoregional control (LRC) and overall survival (OS). However, many patients are unfit for cCRT and receive sequential chemoradiation therapy (sCRT); in this setting, hypofractionated radiation therapy may reduce treatment time, counter tumor repopulation, and improve access.

sections.title: 主要结果
sections.text:
《Optimizing Access in Locally Advanced Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: Hypofractionated Radiation Therapy as a Resource-Efficient Alternative to Conventional Schedules》：结果的原文依据；数值与适用人群以引文为准。

【Results · abstract-3-1】After a median follow-up of 19.6 months, OS, progression-free survival, and distant failure-free survival were comparable among groups. LRC was significantly higher with HYPO-S (62.0%) than with CONV-S (34.8%; p = .009) and similar to CONV-C (62.0%). In multivariate analysis, LRC with HYPO-S remained comparable to CONV-C (p = .576), whereas CONV-S was associated with inferior LRC compared with HYPO-S (hazard ratio, 2.257; 95% CI, 1.046-4.867; p = .038). Toxicity profiles were acceptable, with no significant differences in rates of grade ≥2 esophagitis or pneumonitis across groups.

【Conclusions · abstract-4-1】Sequential hypofractionated chemoradiation therapy achieved LRC and OS comparable to cCRT and superior LRC compared with sequential conventional schedules, without increased toxicity. These findings support broader adoption of HYPO-S as a resource-efficient, clinically effective strategy for patients ineligible for cCRT, particularly in low-income and middle-income health care systems.
